subject: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice
messages:
From: Maria Gutierrez <maria.gutierrez@novushealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team asked me to follow up with a few specific asks so we can move the procurement conversation forward for a private deployment (VPC + on-prem hybrid):

- We need explicit language about data residency: can you confirm which components/processors will see plaintext customer data when running in our VPC vs. Redwood-managed control plane?
- Customer-managed keys: we want to own the CMK (no escrow) but accept a small operator break-glass for emergency support. What is Redwood's standard liability allocation if operator access is used?
- Subprocessor notice: please provide the current list of subprocessors that would have any access (even indirect) to telemetry or logs from private deployments and the notification window for changes.

If you can share a short summary and a redline of the DPA excerpt you propose, that would help legal. We are aiming to finalize terms by the end of the month.

Regards,
Maria
Senior Counsel, Novus Health

(Attachment: Novus-questions-061026.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gutierrez <maria.gutierrez@novushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Laura (legal) and our security lead Kim so we can respond with specifics and a short DPA excerpt. High level:

- Data residency: in a VPC/on-prem hybrid, customer data and model inputs remain in your VPC/air-gapped environment. Redwood's control plane will only see metadata necessary for orchestration unless you opt into usage analytics; we can mark that in the DPA.
- CMK options: BYOK with no escrow is supported; we do offer an optional operator break-glass flow that requires multi-party approval and an auditable ticket. We will propose liability caps tied to direct damages for operator-initiated disclosures.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current list; we notify customers 30 days in advance for any material changes to subprocessors that could affect telemetry.

I'll let Laura and Kim provide the redline and technical notes. Expect an internal draft in ~24 hours and a consolidated reply to you by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(References: internal ticket #RD-9223)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Maria Gutierrez <maria.gutierrez@novushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice

Maria / Karthik — Laura here from Legal. Quick overview and proposed contract positions so Novus can decide what works:

1) Data residency and access scopes
- We will add a DPA schedule that enumerates components and their access tier (e.g., Control Plane: metadata-only; Serving Nodes: plaintext for inference within customer VPC; Operator Tools: telemetry/metrics only).
- For on-prem-only installs we can contractually limit Redwood personnel access to exception-based remote support flows.

2) Keys and break-glass
- BYOK: customer retains sole cryptographic control; Redwood will not escrow keys by default.
- Break-glass: available as an addendum requiring 2-person approval from Redwood on-call + a named Novus admin trigger. We propose operator actions be logged, forensics delivered within 72 hours, and liability for such operator access limited to direct damages up to the value of 6 months of paid service.

3) Subprocessors and notification
- Current subprocessors that interact with private deployments are limited (see attached list). We propose 30 days' notice for any changes that materially affect telemetry or data access; for high-risk additions (e.g., third-party observability vendors) we will obtain either customer approval or offer an alternative isolation path.

I'll attach a redline of the relevant DPA excerpt and placeholder language for the break-glass addendum. Happy to jump on a short call with Novus counsel to walk through.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: dpa-draft-redwood-privdep-excerpt.pdf)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice

Hi all — Kim from Security. A few operational clarifications to support the legal language and make the break-glass practical:

- Operator access flow: we enforce a time-limited support session via ephemeral bastion with MFA and session recording. The break-glass ticket must include JIRA id and a root-cause statement. We can require a signed Novus acceptance of a support-runbook before enabling.
- Key management: recommend adding explicit KMS rotation and retention windows in the runbook. If Novus wants no escrow, we will provide a documented remote-restore procedure for agent upgrades that does not require key material exchange (agent reload via signed artifacts).
- Telemetry minimization: we will redact request payloads from any outbound telemetry by default and retain only token-level latency/size metrics unless you opt-in to richer traces.

I'll attach the ops appendix with the escape procedures and a sample audit extract so legal can see the level of evidence available.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: ops-runbook-escrow-appendix.docx)

Subject: Re: Private deployment: data territory, keystore liability & subprocessor notice

Maria — thanks for the patience. Summarizing the agreed positions from Redwood that we can move into a DPA redline and a short addendum:

1) Data territory
- Serving nodes located inside Novus's VPC/on-prem will process plaintext inference data. Redwood control plane will be limited to orchestration metadata unless Novus explicitly enables aggregated usage analytics.

2) Keys and break-glass
- BYOK by default, no escrow. Optional break-glass requires 2-party Redwood approval and a Novus admin trigger. Break-glass access will be logged and forensics provided within 72 hours. Liability for operator-initiated disclosures capped at direct damages up to six months' fees (we can negotiate that cap).

3) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors provided in the attached list; Redwood will give 30 days' notice for additions that affect telemetry or data access and will not add a subprocessor that directly seeds customer plaintext outside of the VPC without Novus approval.

Next steps: Laura will circulate a redline DPA excerpt (attached) and Kim's ops appendix shows the audit artifacts we can share during onboarding. If these positions look acceptable, can we schedule a call Thursday next week with Novus counsel to finalize redlines?

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: dpa-draft-redwood-privdep-excerpt.pdf, ops-runbook-escrow-appendix.docx)
